365179.title: Ogg's conjecture on the Shimura subgroup of J_0(p)
365179.statement:
Let $p$ be prime. Let $\mathcal{S}(p)$ be the Shimura subgroup of $J_0(p)$, and let $\mathcal{M}(p)$ be the largest $\mu$-type subgroup of $J_0(p)$. **Ogg's Shimura-subgroup conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{S}(p)=\mathcal{M}(p).
$$

This is the dual counterpart of Ogg's cuspidal torsion conjecture. The source says that Mazur proved it using properties of the Eisenstein ideal and the Gorenstein property of the relevant Hecke algebras.

365214.title: Drton–Sturmfels–Sullivant conjecture on the ML-degree of cycle graphs
365214.statement:

$$
\MLdeg(C_n)=(n-3)\cdot 2^{n-2}+1.
$$

This conjecture predicts the observed ML-degrees of cycle graphs and gives an explicit formula for their algebraic statistical complexity. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been proved or disproved.

365298.title: Schmeichel's basis-number conjecture for toroidal graphs
365298.statement:
A graph $G$ is **toroidal** if it can be embedded on the torus, and its **basis number** $\operatorname{bn}(G)$ is the smallest integer $k$ for which $G$ has a cycle-space basis in which every edge belongs to at most $k$ basis elements. **Schmeichel's conjecture.** Every toroidal graph has basis number $3$, that is,

$$
\operatorname{bn}(G)=3.
$$

This conjecture extends MacLane's characterization of planar graphs, for which the basis number is $2$, to graphs embeddable on the torus. Schmeichel proved the general upper bound $\operatorname{bn}(G)\leq 2g+2$ for graphs of genus $g$, but the stated toroidal case is not resolved in the supplied source.

365332.title: Levi-Hadwiger illumination conjecture
365332.statement:
Let $n\ge 2$ and let $K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body. The illumination number $\operatorname{ill}(K)$ is the minimum number of directions needed to illuminate $K$.

**Levi-Hadwiger illumination conjecture.** We have

$$
\operatorname{ill}(K)\le 2^n.
$$

Moreover, equality holds if and only if $K$ is an affine image of the hypercube.

By Boltyanski's equivalence, this is equivalent to the Levi-Hadwiger covering problem, which asks whether every convex body can be covered by at most $2^n$ translates of its interior, with equality only for affine images of the hypercube. The conjecture is unresolved in general.
365332.investigation: Real convex-body illumination problem retained; source mainly treats complex analogues. No feasible all-dimensional mechanism. No new current-status claim.

365358.title: Böttcher–Hladký–Piguet–Taraz tree-packing conjecture

365384.title: Hamiltonicity threshold conjecture via linear forests
365384.statement:
Let $n$ be even, let $\alpha\in(0,1/2)$ be fixed, and set $d=\alpha n$. Let $H_n$ be the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $d$ and $n-d$.

A linear forest in the random graph on the larger part can be incorporated into a Hamilton cycle of the perturbed complete bipartite graph. The paper does not give an explicit threshold because the size of the largest linear forest in a sparse random graph has not been determined in the literature.

365385.title: Hamiltonicity threshold conjecture for randomly perturbed directed graphs
365385.statement:

365401.title: Zhu et al.'s five-color conjecture for generalized Petersen graphs
365401.statement:

$$
\chi^\prime_s(GP(n,k))\leq 5.
$$

365436.title: Equality of the sorting classes for the 312-type stack-sorting maps
365436.statement:

$$
\text{Sort}_n(\text{SC}_{312})=\text{Sort}_n(\text{SC}_{\underline{31}2})=\text{Sort}_n(\text{SC}_{3\underline{12}}).
$$

Furthermore, for every $\tau\in\text{Sort}_n(\text{SC}_{312})$,

$$
\text{SC}_{312}(\tau)=\text{SC}_{\underline{31}2}(\tau)=\text{SC}_{3\underline{12}}(\tau).
$$

The maps $\text{SC}_{\underline{31}2}$ and $\text{SC}_{3\underline{12}}$ are being compared because their sorting-class cardinalities agree in the computed cases and the corresponding classical and vincular maps coincide in related free-stack situations. The equality of the classes and of their values on the sorting class remains conjectural.

365555.title: The Tijdeman–Zagier conjecture for products
365555.statement:
Let $x,y,n,m,d,s$ be positive integers, with $x$ and $y$ coprime. A **product of degree $d$ and spread $s$** is a product of $d$ positive integers whose maximum minus minimum is $s$.

**Tijdeman–Zagier conjecture for products.** The integer $x^n\pm y^m$ is not a product of degree $d$ satisfying

$$
2<d\leq\min(n,m)
$$

and of spread $s$ satisfying

$$
\frac{1}{n}+\frac{1}{m}+\frac{1+s}{d}<1.
$$

This generalizes the classical Tijdeman–Zagier, or Beal, conjecture by permitting the third term to be a product rather than a single power. The paper reports computational testing but no proof or disproof, so the conjecture remains open.

365633.title: The commutativity conjectures for strong Lie algebras
365633.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $L$ be an $n$-strong Lie algebra over a field with at least $n$ elements, and let $A(L)$ be its universal enveloping algebra. For a monomial $p(x_1,\ldots,x_s)$, its multiweight records the degree in each variable. **Strong-Lie-algebra commutativity conjectures.** The following assertions should hold: (I) for all Lie elements $a,b\in A(L)$,

$$
a^{n-1}b^{n-1}=(-1)^{n-1}b^{n-1}a^{n-1};
$$
 (II) for every monomial $p(x,y)$ of multiweight $(n-1,n-1)$ and all Lie elements $a,b\in A(L)$,

$$
p(a,b)=(-1)^{n-1}p(b,a);
$$
 (III) for every monomial $p(x_1,\ldots,x_s)$ of multiweight $(n-1,\ldots,n-1)$, every collection of Lie elements $a_i\in A(L)$, and every permutation $\sigma$, the elements $p(a_1,\ldots,a_s)$ and $p(a_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,a_{\sigma(s)})$ are $\mathbb{F}_p$-linearly dependent. These conjectures seek a commutativity phenomenon in the enveloping algebras of strong Lie algebras; the source reports verification of the first identity for small values but leaves the general assertions conjectural.
365633.investigation: Need n-strong Lie algebra adjoint-operator interpretation of A(L), not arbitrary elements of an unrestricted associative algebra. Source Conjecture 4.8 and subsequent conditional proof do not resolve general multiweight identities. PBW or scalar-unity counterexamples without semantic bridge are invalid.

365687.title: The isolation-number lower-bound conjectures
365687.statement:
For a graph $G$, let ${\rm iso}(G,k)$ be the maximum number of pairwise disjoint $k$-clique isolating sets in a partition of $V(G)$, and let ${\rm iso}_c(G)$ be the analogous number for cycle isolating sets. **The isolation-number lower-bound conjectures.** (i) If $k \geq 3$ and $G$ is connected with $G \ncong K_k$, then

$$
{\rm iso}(G,k) \geq k+1.
$$

(ii) If $G$ is connected with $G \ncong C_3$, then

$$
{\rm iso}_c(G) \geq 4.
$$
 These are explicitly stated to be equivalent to the two partition conjectures above, so they do not constitute additional independent claims.

365746.title: Pullman's conjecture on strongly consistent odd-regular graphs
365746.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite undirected graph. An **orientation** of $G$ is obtained by directing each edge, and $G$ is **strongly consistent** if every orientation of $G$ is consistent, where consistency means that the minimum number of directed paths in an edge decomposition equals the excess

$$
\operatorname{ex}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{v\in V(D)}\lvert d^+(v)-d^-(v)\rvert.
$$

**Pullman's conjecture.** For odd $d$, every $d$-regular graph is strongly consistent. This generalizes the even-order tournament conjecture from complete graphs to all odd-regular graphs; the paper develops results for sparse graphs but does not resolve the conjecture in full.

365773.title: Small-representative conjecture for sum-product pairs
365773.statement:

$$
\operatorname{SPP}(n)=\{(|A+A|,|AA|):A\subseteq\mathbb N,\ |A|=n\},

$$
A+A=\{a+b:a,b\in A\},\qquad AA=\{ab:a,b\in A\}.

$$
|A|=n,\qquad |A+A|=i,\qquad |AA|=j,
$$

and

$$
\max A\le 2^{\left\lfloor(3n-4)/2\right\rfloor}.
$$

365858.title: Regular-subhypergraph conjecture for linear hypergraphs
365858.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ be an integer, let $\lambda\geq 1$, and let a **$k$-uniform linear hypergraph** be a hypergraph in which every edge has $k$ vertices and any two distinct edges intersect in at most one vertex. $$
r\geq cd.
$$

The conjecture would extend the paper's regularisation results from graphs to linear hypergraphs. The authors note that the needed hypergraph analogue of the Alon--Friedland--Kalai result is unknown, which is why the extension is conjectural.

365893.title: Ghosh's regular-sequence conjecture for the Casas–Alvero problem
365893.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let $n$ be a positive integer, and set $R=K[x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}]$. For $j\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $\Phi_j:R\to R$ be given by $\Phi_j(x_i)=x_i-x_j$ for $i\neq j$ and $\Phi_j(x_j)=-x_j$, while $\Phi_n$ is the identity. Let $\sigma_i(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ be the $i$-th elementary symmetric function, set $\mathcal T=\{1,\ldots,n\}^{n-1}$, and for $T=(j_1,\ldots,j_{n-1})\in\mathcal T$ define $G_{T,i}=\Phi_{j_i}(\sigma_i(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}))$. **Ghosh's regular-sequence conjecture.** For every choice of $T\in\mathcal T$, the sequence of homogeneous polynomials

$$
(G_{T,1},\ldots,G_{T,n-1})
$$

forms a regular sequence in $R$. This is an equivalent algebraic formulation of the Casas–Alvero conjecture over arbitrary fields. The paper attributes this formulation to Soham Ghosh; its general validity remains open.

365926.title: Type-and-Jordan-type invariance conjecture for unitary stable orbital integral strata
365926.statement:
Let $L$ be a unimodular hermitian lattice over the ring of integers $\boldsymbol{o}_E$ of an unramified quadratic extension $E/F$, and let $M,M'$ be sublattices of $L$. Write $\mathcal{SO}_{\gamma,M}$ for the volume of the stratum associated with $M$, and suppose that $M$ and $M'$ have the same type and the same Jordan type. **Type-and-Jordan-type invariance conjecture.** Then

$$
\mathcal{SO}_{\gamma,M}=\mathcal{SO}_{\gamma,M'}.
$$

This asserts that these two discrete invariants determine the stratum volume in the unitary case. The supplied text gives no resolution status or further evidence.

365948.title: Liu's modified degree-sequence conjecture for extremal nonregular graphs
365948.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}(n,\Delta)$ be the set of connected nonregular graphs of order $n$ with maximum degree $\Delta$ that attain the maximum spectral radius. Suppose $\Delta\geq 3$ and $G\in\mathcal{G}(n,\Delta)$. For each fixed $\Delta$ and sufficiently large $n$, write the degree sequence of $G$ as $(\Delta,\ldots,\Delta,\delta)$. **Liu's modified conjecture.** The exceptional degree is

$$
\delta=\begin{cases}
\Delta-1,&\text{if }\Delta\text{ and }n\text{ are both odd},\\
1,&\text{if }\Delta\text{ is odd and }n\text{ is even},\\
\Delta-2,&\text{if }\Delta\text{ is even}.
\end{cases}
$$

This is a modification of the Liu–Li conjecture after the cases $\Delta=3,4$ were confirmed. The source presents the modified statement as a conjecture; its general resolution is not supplied.

365979.title: Rainbow Hamilton cycle conjecture for bounded edge-colourings of Dirac graphs
365979.statement: Let $G$ be a **Dirac graph** on $n$ vertices, meaning a graph with minimum degree at least $n/2$, and let its edge-colouring be **proper** if every pair of incident edges receives different colours. The colouring is **$n/8$-bounded** if each colour is assigned to at most $n/8$ edges. A Hamilton cycle is **rainbow** if all its edges receive distinct colours. **Rainbow Hamilton cycle conjecture.** There exists a rainbow Hamilton cycle in any proper $n/8$-bounded edge-colouring of a Dirac graph on $n$ vertices. The paper proves near-rainbow results and shows that the constant $1/8$ is best possible up to lower-order terms, leaving the exact $n/8$-bounded assertion open.

365982.title: The logarithmic edge-bound conjecture for planar spanning-tree numbers
365982.statement:
Let $\beta(t)$ be the smallest number of edges of a planar graph, allowing multiple edges, with exactly $t$ spanning trees. It is known that $\beta(t)=O(\log t\,\log\log t)$. **Logarithmic edge-bound conjecture.**

365988.title: The degree-two bound for irreducible polynomial integrals on the two-torus
365988.statement: Let the geodesic flow be the Hamiltonian flow of a Riemannian metric on the 2-torus. A polynomial first integral is a polynomial in the momenta that Poisson-commutes with the Hamiltonian, and it is **irreducible** if it is not generated as a nontrivial polynomial expression by lower-degree first integrals. **The degree-two bound conjecture.** The largest possible degree of any irreducible polynomial first integral of the geodesic flow on the 2-torus is not larger than $2$. 366017.title: Exponential upper-bound conjecture for the three-uniform color-avoiding Ramsey function
366017.statement:
Let $R_3(n;3,2)$ be the least integer $N$ such that every three-coloring of the edges of the complete three-uniform hypergraph $K_N^{(3)}$ contains a copy of $K_n^{(3)}$ using at most two colors. **Exponential upper-bound conjecture.** There exists a constant $c>0$ such that

$$
R_3(n;3,2)\leq 2^{n^c}.
$$

The corresponding color-avoiding problem is open, and even in uniformity three the quantitative behavior for $r=3$ and $s=2$ is poorly understood. Existing methods give an exponential-type lower bound and a double-exponential upper bound, so the conjecture would substantially improve the known upper bound and determine the tower height.

366047.title: The tropical minimum conjecture for theta-function combinations
366047.statement:
Let $\Theta_v$ be the theta functions indexed by the relevant tropical points, and let $a_v$ be non-zero coefficients. $$
\left(\sum a_v\Theta_v\right)^{\mathrm{trop}}=\min \Theta_v^{\mathrm{trop}}.
$$

366076.title: Tian's strong stabilization conjecture for alpha-invariants
366076.statement:
Let $X$ be a projective manifold and let $L$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Define the section ring

$$
R(X,L):=\bigoplus_{k=0}^{\infty}H^0(X,kL).
$$

The quantities $\alpha(L)$ and $\alpha_k(L)$ denote respectively the global and level $k$ log canonical thresholds.

**Tian's strong stabilization conjecture.** If $R(X,L)$ is generated by

$$
\bigoplus_{k=0}^{k_0}H^0(X,kL),
$$

then, for every $k\geq k_0$,

$$
\alpha_k(L)=\alpha(L).
$$

In particular, if $R(X,L)$ is generated by $H^0(X,L)$, then, for every $k\in\mathbb{N}_+$,

$$
\alpha_k(L)=\alpha(L).
$$

This is a stronger form of Tian's stabilization conjecture because it predicts an explicit stabilization threshold from generators of the section ring. A counterexample was provided by Ahmadinezhad, Cheltsov, and Schicho, so the conjecture is refuted.

366095.title: The layered-permutation conjecture for maximal Newton-polytope support
366095.statement:
For $n\geq 1$, let $\theta_w$ denote the number of supports of the Schubert polynomial $\mathfrak{S}_w(x)$, equivalently the number of lattice points in its Newton polytope, and define

$$
\beta_n=\max\{\theta_w\colon w\in S_n\}.
$$

A **layered permutation** is a concatenation of decreasing blocks on consecutive intervals. **Layered-maximizer conjecture.** For $n\geq 1$, the permutations in $S_n$ attaining the maximum value $\beta_n$ are layered permutations. This is equivalent to saying that the permutations whose Newton polytopes have the largest number of lattice points are layered permutations; the source reports verification for $n$ up to $9$.

366096.title: Gao's positivity conjecture for permutation-pattern coefficients
366096.statement:
For $w\in S_n$, write

$$
\nu_w=1+\sum_{u\in S_m\atop m\leq n}c_u\,p_u(w),
$$

where $p_u(w)$ counts occurrences of the pattern $u$ in $w$, and define the coefficients recursively by

$$
c_u=\nu_u-1-\sum_{\sigma\in S_\ell\atop \ell<m}c_\sigma\,p_\sigma(u).
$$

Here $u$ ranges over permutations and $c_u$ has the stability property $c_u=0$ when the final entry of $u$ is its maximum. **Gao's positivity conjecture.** For any permutation $u$, $c_u\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. The source records proofs for several pattern-avoidance classes, but not the general assertion.

366167.title: The low-power error-correcting cooling code density conjecture
366167.statement:
Let $t$ and $w$ be fixed, and let $C(n,t,w,w-2)$ denote the maximum size of an $(n,t,w,w-2)$-LPECC code. Assume

$$
(t+1)w(w-1)<(w+t)(w+t-1).
$$

**Low-power error-correcting cooling code density conjecture.** Under this condition,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{C(n,t,w,w-2)}{n^2}=\frac{1}{(t+1)w(w-1)},
$$

or, more strongly,

$$
C(n,t,w,w-2)=\left\lfloor\frac{(n+1)n}{(t+1)w(w-1)}\right\rfloor
$$

for infinitely many $n$ with fixed $w$ and $t$. The conjecture proposes that the lower-bound density is asymptotically optimal, and that the stronger exact value is attained infinitely often; the source gives no resolution.

366168.title: Tait's extremal $A_0$-spectral radius conjecture for $K_{a,b}$-minor-free graphs

366231.title: Grünbaum's digon conjecture for pairwise crossing pseudocircles
366231.statement:
Let a **pseudocircle** be a simple closed Jordan curve in the plane, and let an **arrangement** be the cell complex into which the plane is decomposed by a family of pseudocircles. An arrangement is **simple** if no point lies on three pseudocircles. A **digon** is a face bounded by exactly two edges.

**Grünbaum's digon conjecture.** Every simple arrangement of $n>2$ pairwise crossing pseudocircles has at most $2n-2$ digons.

This is the simple-arrangement formulation of Grünbaum's conjecture that the maximum for nontrivial arrangements of pairwise crossing pseudocircles is $2n-2$; the source provides no resolution status.

366257.statement: Let $G$ be an Eulerian oriented planar graph, meaning a connected oriented planar graph in which every vertex has even degree.
